clue.text: Change into suit

definitions.meaning: to turn into something, as a caterpillar turns into a butterfly
to look good on, as a hat may flatter its wearer

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get changed into a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both senses: to grow into a new state, and to flatter or look right on someone.

clue.text: Was the president a very immature primate?

parts.note: George Bush, and his son George W Bush, were US presidents
a baby is as immature as can be

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a US president was a childish ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Galagos, small big-eyed African nocturnal animals, are primates related to lemurs.

clue.text: Prisoners concealing heavy defeat are in the soup

indicators.note: concealing means the prisoners wrap round and hide the word for the defeat

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: Prisoners hide a heavy defeat and find themselves in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' looks like the idiom for being in trouble, but it is literal: the answer is the fried bread cubes floating in soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Small cubes of fried or toasted bread are things that float in a bowl of broth.

clue.text: Fish in the sky?

parts.note: a sky dappled with rippled cloud is named after the patterned scales of a sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether there are fish up in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fish with a striped back gives its name to a dappled cloud pattern overhead.

clue.text: Undertaker's singular charity during most of three months

definitions.note: the possessive 's stands for 'is': the undertaker is the wordplay that follows

indicators.note: during means the charity word sits inside the shared month ending

parts.note: September, November and December all end in the same five letters, most of each month's name
alms are charity; one alm is the singular form

explanation.surface: An undertaker's one-off donation is spread across most of the autumn months.
explanation.walkthrough: Undertaker's here reads 'undertaker is'. The singular ALM is a crossword back-formation from alms.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who preserves bodies for burial does the work of a funeral director.

clue.text: Din Mog the cat made was Stanislavsky's idea

indicators.note: made here means the letters are worked into something new, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written; Mog is a common British name for a cat

explanation.surface: The racket made by Mog the cat illustrated a theatre director's theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' signals the anagram of all twelve letters of DIN MOG THE CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Konstantin Stanislavsky devised the system of performance in which a player lives the role's emotions.

clue.text: See 5
Not a lot of silver in the lake

indicators.note: in puts the symbol for silver inside the word for the lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: There is very little silver to be found in the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant or paltry: the adjective describes an amount that is small.

clue.text: Nursery versery?

parts.note: a made-up plural of verse, read as the poems for small children that sound alike at line ends

explanation.surface: A jokey coinage for little verses sung in the nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's verses known as nursery songs are built on words with matching sounds.

clue.text: See 11
Figures at a rusty exhibition

indicators.note: an exhibition puts things on show in a new arrangement, so these letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some old figures are on show at a rather corroded exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhibition' signals the anagram: the eight letters of AT A RUSTY are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Statues collectively are sculpted figures; the word names a body of statues.

clue.text: Goat to put a stop to toffee

parts.note: a goat is an animal that butts, so a cryptic 'one who butts'
to scotch a rumour or plan is to stop it

explanation.surface: A goat is told to stop eating toffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goat' is not the definition: it is a playful description, one who butts. The answer is a brittle sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard sweet made from butter and brown sugar is a classic kind of toffee.

clue.text: Fleet before moving about, like Elsa the lion cub

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround the navy abbreviation
moving shifts the letters of the word before into a new order

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's fleet

explanation.surface: A navy fleet sets off before something else moves about, all in the manner of a famous lioness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' scrambles the word before, and 'about' wraps it round the fleet. Elsa was the lioness raised by Joy Adamson, subject of a 1960 book and 1966 film.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsa the lioness was raised by humans and released to the wild, famously told in a book and film of that title.

clue.text: Second left for weird gorge, according to commentator

parts.note: B denotes second class or second grade, as in a B-list

indicators.note: something weird is strange and twisted, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A commentator reports on someone who came second and left for a strange ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' signals an anagram of B, L and the letters of GORGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes an online journal is a modern commentator on events.

clue.text: Sausage past sell-by date? Will it pass its MOT?

definitions.meaning: a stale sausage, ... being British slang for a sausage
a battered car whose roadworthiness is in doubt; the MOT is the UK's annual vehicle safety test

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a stale sausage could pass a roadworthiness test.
explanation.walkthrough: BANGER is British slang both for a sausage and for a decrepit car; the MOT is the UK's annual test of a vehicle's roadworthiness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a worn-out car in slang, and read literally a sausage that has gone stale.

clue.text: See 13
Haphazard extended to monk

parts.note: a road that ran a mile extended a mile
Dom is a title given to certain monks, such as Benedictines

explanation.surface: Something haphazard stretched as far as a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without method or pattern means arbitrary, the same as aimless chance.

clue.text: See 15
Love in a monkey causes dreamy inactivity

indicators.note: in tells us the zero-shaped letter is placed inside the name of the monkey

parts.note: a langur is an Asian monkey
love is zero in tennis, and zero is the letter O

explanation.surface: Being in love with a monkey leaves someone dreamily idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude, a pleasant listless torpor, is exactly what the word describes.

clue.text: Strong flavour of partly ripe game containing nitrogen

indicators.note: partly means only some of the word ripe is used, its last two letters dropped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: containing means the board game wraps round the symbol for nitrogen

parts.note: chess is a board game
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A strong taste comes from partly ripened game with nitrogen added.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's game is meat for the table, not a pastime; 'partly' keeps only the first half of ripe.
explanation.definitionFit: Fullness and depth of taste in food is described as its opulence.

clue.text: Extra plug to study a lot of Dumas

parts.note: a plug is a piece of advertising, an ad
a den is a private study

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the name is used, its end dropped

parts.note: taken as written; Alexandre Dumas was the French novelist

explanation.surface: An extra promotion is added to research into much of Dumas's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last two letters of DUMAS, leaving DUM.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix added to a book or document is a supplement, something extra.

clue.text: Listen taking in heartless saying to boater, say

indicators.note: taking in means the word for listen surrounds the shortened proverb

parts.note: to hear is to listen

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the word for saying

parts.note: an adage is a proverb or saying

explanation.surface: Someone hears a pointless proverb addressed to a person in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A boater is a flat straw hat, not someone rowing, so 'say' marks it as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A boater is a stiff flat straw hat, one example of something worn on the head.

clue.text: Epicene county?

definitions.meaning: having characteristics of both ..., a ... in between
a former English county around London

explanation.surface: A county is described as being of indeterminate gender.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer means an in-between gender, which is what epicene means; as one word it is the old English county that held much of north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicene means sharing traits of both sexes, an in-between gender; the single word names a historic English home county.

clue.text: Result of raising gun?

parts.note: raising means lifting up
a shot is a marksman, as in a good shot, a gun

explanation.surface: Someone asks what came of lifting a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome or consequence of events is their upshot.

clue.text: From wet nurse onwards-foreign office's expression's different

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office; with its possessive s, FOS
a term is an expression or word; the 's here is 'is'
other means different

explanation.surface: From the nurse onwards, the Foreign Office's way of speaking is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' and 'onwards' only link the surface; the definition is the nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet nurse breastfeeds a child not her own, acting as its substitute parent.

clue.text: See 23
See 21
Home counties island? Not quite mustn't go any further

parts.note: SE is South East, the region of England where the home counties around London lie

indicators.note: not quite means the island's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: An island near the home counties is nearly kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Something confidential must not be passed on beyond the people who know it.

clue.text: Lord of the ring, perhaps, needs more port

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are needed, in a fresh arrangement, to make the boxing figure

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boxing impresario demands extra fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord of the ring' suggests Tolkien, but it means the boss of a boxing ring; the eight letters of MORE PORT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing impresario who stages fights is in effect the ruler of the ring.

clue.text: Prepare to sew in city street

definitions.meaning: pass the yarn through the eye of the sewing tool before stitching
a street in the City of London, home of the Bank of England

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready to stitch while in a street in town.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district; its street of this name houses the Bank of England, the 'Old Lady' of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Threading the eye of the tool is the first step before stitching; the same phrase names the London street of the Bank of England.

clue.text: Shells burst here (hard one, the cry goes out)

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
A means one, as in a single item

indicators.note: the cry goes out, scattered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shells explode in a place where a hard cry rings out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes out' signals an anagram of THE CRY, giving TCHERY after H and A. The shells are eggshells breaking, not artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: In a place where eggs are incubated, chicks break out of their shells.

clue.text: See 27
Compound paintings right in gallery

indicators.note: in puts the art and the right-hand letter inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: A mixture of paintings is hung on the right side of a gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt of tartaric acid is a chemical compound, such as cream of tartar.

clue.text: Compound of alkali, some reckon

indicators.note: of here means a part of, so the answer is taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: Some people reckon this compound is made of an alkali.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across alkalI SOME Reckon.
explanation.definitionFit: A molecule with the same atoms as another but arranged differently is a chemical compound of a special kind.
